history.period: Established 1501 CE by Maharaja Dhanya Manikya (r. 1490-1520)
history.summary: CSV town 'Udaipur' accepted with refinement: the shrine stands at Matabari on the south-western outskirts of Udaipur town, Gomati district. This is the famous Matabari Shakti Peetha, one of the 51 Shakti Peethas (legend: Sati's right foot / Dakshin Charan with the big toe fell here). Built in 1501 CE by Maharaja Dhanya Manikya in the Bengali Ek-ratna style - a small cubical edifice (24 sq ft base, 75 ft high) on a hillock shaped like a tortoise hump (Kurma Pitha / Kurmaprishthakriti). The state of Tripura is named after this temple. The sanctum holds two black-stone idols: the 5-ft Tripura Sundari and the 2-ft Chhoto-Ma (Chandi), which the kings carried to battlefields and hunts; Kalyan Sagar lake (east) shelters rare bostami turtles. Legend: the king had a dream of the Goddess directing worship on the hillock where a Vishnu temple already stood - hence its syncretic Shakta-Vaishnava character. The famous Diwali Mela draws lakhs of pilgrims. Animal sacrifice was banned Oct 2019 and resumed Dec 2019 after a 57-day ban (per Wikipedia - verify current status). The complex was redeveloped under the PRASHAD scheme and a 51-Shakti Peethas Park is coming up at Banduar ~4 km away. This file deliberately uses a distinct id ('tripureshwari-temple-matabari-udaipur') to satisfy id uniqueness pending the coordinator's merge.

name: Tripura Sundari Temple
town: Matabari, Udaipur (CSV town 'Udaipur' is the broader ancient city; the temple is at Matabari on the south-western outskirts of Udaipur town)
town_description: Udaipur, in Gomati district on the Gomati river about 55 km from Agartala, was the capital of the Tripura kingdom under the Manikya dynasty before the capital shifted to Agartala. It is a cluster of 16th-17th century Manikya temples: the Shakti Peetha of Tripura Sundari at Matabari, the Bhuvaneswari temple by the Gomati, the Gunabati group of brick temples, and the old stone Jagannath temple by Jagannath Dighi.
